title: Trail and Rivergate
premise: Casper Halloran, a railroad engineer hiding from a past scandal, is drawn into a rescue expedition when a dying prospector trades a map of closed mountain lines for a promise to bring his crew home. Leading the party through the wilderness, Casper discovers the prospector's crew found something worth killing for: evidence that the railroad's own directors buried a town and its people to cover a catastrophic bridge failure. As the expedition's wealthy backer schemes to seize and destroy the proof, Casper must choose between the invisibility he craves and the justice the dead deserve. In the end, he sacrifices his anonymity, testifying at great personal cost, and finds a new family among the survivors who choose to stand with him.
about_author: Casper Nystrom is a former surveyor who spent a decade mapping remote rail corridors across the northern ranges before turning to fiction. He writes adventure stories about ordinary people forced to become extraordinary by terrain, weather, and other people's greed.

chapters.title: The Man at Mile Forty-Three
chapters.summary: Third-person limited on Casper Halloran. While surveying a closed line, Casper finds a prospector gut-shot and dying in the snow. The man presses a worn map into his hands and extracts a promise: bring my crew out alive. The beat is reluctant duty; Casper wants no part of anyone's troubles.

chapters.title: A Map of Closed Lines
chapters.summary: Casper studies the map in his cabin, recognizing routes officially abandoned after the Rivergate Bridge collapse five years ago. The dead man's notes reference a camp still holding out beyond the washout. Emotional beat: curiosity overriding self-preservation as he decides to go.

chapters.title: The Backer
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Aldous Vane, the expedition financier, who has quietly bought up claims around Rivergate and needs the prospector's map before anyone else reads it. He hires Casper without revealing why. Beat: menace beneath civility; the reader sees what Casper cannot.

chapters.title: Six Strangers and a Mule
chapters.summary: Back to Casper. The expedition assembles: Vane's nephew Tom, a gruff cook named Ida, two hired guides, a young photographer, and Casper leading. First miles of trail establish friction and competence. Beat: wary camaraderie forming among people with secrets.

chapters.title: The Washout
chapters.summary: The party reaches the collapsed trestle that killed the Rivergate crews. Casper notices the wreckage doesn't match the official report—the piers were cut, not failed. Beat: dread; the wilderness isn't the only thing hiding bodies.

chapters.title: Ida's Kitchen
chapters.summary: Quiet interlude at camp. Ida, it emerges, lost her brother at Rivergate and joined the expedition to find where he fell. She and Casper bond over shared grief kept private. Beat: found family taking root over coffee and honesty.

chapters.title: Tom Vane's Ambition
chapters.summary: Tom POV. Vane has ordered him to steal the map once the camp is reached and let the guides take any blame for accidents. Tom resents being his uncle's instrument but fears him more. Beat: corruption spreading down the chain of command.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: A storm pins the expedition against a cliff face for three days. A guide breaks his leg; Casper rigs a haul system using old rail anchors. Beat: crisis forging trust—Casper stops being an outsider and becomes their leader.

chapters.title: The Camp Beyond the Washout
chapters.summary: They find the prospector's crew: four survivors, half-starved, guarding crates of documents pulled from the river gorge. Their leader, Ruth Okafor, doesn't trust rescuers. Beat: tense negotiation; the truth begins surfacing.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: Ruth shows Casper the evidence: company telegrams ordering the bridge weakened to save costs, then the town evacuated under false pretense and abandoned. Her brother stayed behind to document it. Beat: righteous fury; Casper realizes the promise is bigger than survival.

chapters.title: Vane Arrives
chapters.summary: Vane appears with armed men, claiming he came to help. Privately he offers Casper money and a clean identity in exchange for the documents and silence. Beat: temptation laid bare; Casper refuses, and knows the refusal is a declaration of war.

chapters.title: Night Watch
chapters.summary: Casper and Ruth stand watch together, trading histories—his disgrace, her losses—and admit neither can walk away now. Beat: intimacy and resolve; the found family solidifies around shared purpose rather than circumstance.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Someone cuts the supply ropes and scatters the mules. Suspicion splits the group until Casper proves Tom did it under orders. Tom, cornered, confesses his uncle's plan. Beat: betrayal and fracture, but also the first defector from Vane's side.

chapters.title: The Descent
chapters.summary: Vane's men move to take the camp by force. The expedition flees down the gorge with the documents, using the closed rail line Casper knows better than anyone. Beat: desperate flight; Casper's hidden expertise becomes their lifeline.

chapters.title: Deadman's Tunnel
chapters.summary: Trapped in a tunnel with Vane's men sealing both ends, Casper leads them through a maintenance crawlway only an engineer would find. A guide is lost covering the retreat. Beat: sacrifice; the cost of justice becomes real and personal.

chapters.title: River Crossing
chapters.summary: Spring melt swells the river. They build a raft from tunnel timbers; Ida nearly drowns saving the documents, and Tom pulls her out, choosing his new companions over his bloodline. Beat: loyalty proven in water and terror.

chapters.title: The Trap at Rivergate Station
chapters.summary: Vane anticipates their route and waits at the ruined station with a warrant naming Casper a fugitive murderer—the frame built years ago, dusted off. Beat: despair; the law itself is Vane's weapon.

chapters.title: Turning the Evidence
chapters.summary: Ruth reveals she wired a journalist from the camp weeks ago; the story of Rivergate is already printing. Vane's men waver as the truth goes public. Beat: reversal; justice outside the law arrives through witness, not force.

chapters.title: Confrontation on the Trestle
chapters.summary: Climax. Vane, exposed, tries to burn the remaining originals atop the broken trestle. Casper confronts him; Tom stands with Casper. Vane falls into the gorge he created—by his own hand or the river's, the text leaves uncertain. Beat: catharsis and horror entwined.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: In the territorial court, Casper surrenders his alias and testifies, accepting arrest for his old crime—a forged inspection report he made under duress years ago. Beat: reckoning; he chooses accountability over invisibility.

chapters.title: Sentences
chapters.summary: Casper receives a reduced sentence for cooperation; the others wait for him. Ida buries her brother's name properly; Ruth reopens the claims in the crew's names. Beat: bittersweet justice; the law, imperfect, finally bends toward the dead.

chapters.title: Trail and Rivergate
chapters.summary: Two years later, Caspar—pardoned—runs a small line rebuilt over the gorge, with Ida, Ruth, and Tom beside him. On the anniversary they leave flowers at the trestle. Final beat: the wilderness forgets nothing, but family remembers together.
